content.title: Trader Joe’s Settles $7.4 Million Lawsuit: Here’s How to See If You’re Eligible for Payout
content.text: NEED TO KNOW Customers who used credit or debit cards at Trader Joe's in early 2019 may qualify for a settlement payoutThe $7.4 million settlement addresses a 2019 class action lawsuit claiming that the chain increased risk of identity theft by printing receipts showing too many card digits at some storesClaims must be submitted by June 6, 2026, for estimated payouts of $102.45 per person Trader Joe's is offering a payout to customers as part of a class action settlement. Customers who made a purchase with a credit or debit card between March 5, 2019, and July 19, 2019, may be entitled to a payment due to a class action settlement, according to the settlement's website. In a 2019 complaint obtained by PEOPLE, Brian Keim alleged in a class action lawsuit that Trader Joe's violated the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act (FACTA) amendment to the Fair Credit Reporting Act by printing 10 digits of customers' cards on transaction receipts. Trader Joe's said on the settlement website that no one had reported identity theft from the receipt debacle. “However, identity theft is not required to prove a FACTA claim, and therefore you do not need to have suffered identity theft to submit a claim for payment from this settlement,” the grocery chain added. It also denied the allegations and all liability or wrongdoing, insisting that only a small minority of transactions involved the aforementioned receipts in some stores. The chain wrote that its insurer concluded litigation would be long, expensive and risky, which is why it chose to settle. Trader Joe's noted that the court did not rule on Keim's claims or the case, highlighting that by settling, it was not confirming the validity of Keim's claims. Stock image of a woman looking at a receipt. Getty Per the settlement website, the plaintiff argued that the grocery chain printed receipts that included the first six and last four digits of cards at some of its stores. Keim claimed that these receipts led to a violation of customers' privacy and an increased risk of identity theft. Trader Joe's agreed in the settlement to pay $7.4 million in fees to customers who received receipts showing too many digits between March 5, 2019, and July 19, 2019. The $7.4 million will go towards paying the settlements to those who submit valid and timely claim forms, along with attorneys' fees, reasonable expenses and the costs of notice and administering the settlement. The anticipated attorneys' fees come to about $2.46 million, in addition to an incentive payment of $10,000 to Keim, the website noted. Those who submit a claim will receive a proportional payment distribution calculated by taking the remaining funds for distribution divided by the number of people who submit valid settlement claim forms. The settlement notice said that Keim estimates that the payout for each member will be $102.45. The notice said that those who received an email or postcard regarding the settlement are members of the settlement class. To complete a claim, customers with a Class ID number can submit a claim form to the settlement administrator through the settlement website or over the phone by June 6, 2026. Individuals without a claim ID can submit a claim by entering the first six and last four digits of the card used and the purchase date. Those who submit a claim will lose their right to sue Trader Joe's on the claims of the lawsuit and any claims related to Trader Joe's printing too much information on receipts in the relevant time period. Those who exclude themselves or opt out of the settlement by June 9, 2026, are the only group who will be allowed to continue pursuing such claims against Trader Joe's in the future. Affected individuals can also choose to write to the court about why they think the settlement is unfair. They still must fill out the claim form; however, if they want to receive the benefit. They can also speak to the court at the fairness hearing on Aug. 10, 2026. Those who do nothing will not receive a payment and will give up the right to sue Trader Joe's on the claims, according to the settlement website. Related Stories The notice said that the court must approve the settlement and appeals before payments are made. The hearing to approve the settlement is scheduled for Aug. 10.
